title: Fletcher's wife Leora, trumpeter in the Lafayette pit band
summary: Procope recalls hearing Mrs. Henderson play trumpet in the Lafayette pit; Albertson relays stories about Joe Smith and a women's band, which Procope doesn't know.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: Did you ever hear Fletcher's wife play?

Sure, when I was -- of course I remember hearing her play trumpet. She used to work in the pit band at the Lafayette. Even when I was a little kid I used to go up there and -- of course I didn't know who she was at the time, but then later on I discovered that she was Fletcher Henderson's wife.
She was married to Russell Smith.
At first, right.
Right.
Right.
Then I heard that she was having an affair with Joe Smith and talked Fletcher into hiring Joe.
Well, this I don't know.
Howard Scott told me that, that that's
the way he was fired, because she wanted Joe in the band.
Well, could be. Could be. I mean I'm not saying it isn't so. I mean I'm finding out something, you know.
But she also had a -- she had an all female band at one time.
Well, I don't know --
Called the Vampires. I just wondered if you ever heard that.
No, I don't know that either, no. See, all these people are older than me.
Yes.
Now, I came --
But this was later. This was -- she had a band -- she was in Lil Armstrong's all-woman band in 1933.
Yes.
No, I didn't know about that. No. No.
